items.period: Shuowen ancient-script style; no specific artifact date established
items.tradition: Shuowen ancient script style; modern vector redraw
items.caption: A modern redraw of a 四 form in Shuowen ancient-script style. The upright central stroke separates two looped sides, each with a short inner stroke.
items.alt: Black, symmetrical ancient-script-style glyph with a tall central stroke and two looped sides, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: This candidate gives a clear visual example of a 四 form, while its ancient-script-style label does not establish a specific artifact or date. The sources report competing explanations of 四’s origin, so the drawing alone cannot decide between them.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication; modern SVG representation stated to be public domain.

limitations.text: This modern redraw is not a photograph of an inscription and does not establish when the form was used. The evidence leaves unresolved whether 四 began as a direct numeral graph or was borrowed from a graph associated with 呬.
